---
title: Your first plugin
description: Write a PLUGIN.md plugin with one tool, test it against a recorded response, and share it as a link. The example is a cut-down version of the free-classrooms plugin.
icon: Rocket
---

On this page you write a small plugin document with one tool. The tool answers one question: **how
many classrooms are free in each teaching building right now**. You then test it offline and share
it as a link.

The example is a cut-down version of a real plugin,
[`plugins/classrooms`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins/tree/main/plugins/classrooms)
in the plugins repository. It calls one public campus endpoint, so it needs no login.

Before you start, install [bun](https://bun.sh) and git. You don't need the app or a phone until
the last step.

For the full language, see [Declarative plugins](/en/docs/build/declarative-plugins). The
specification itself is
[`PLUGIN-LANGUAGE.md`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness/blob/master/docs/PLUGIN-LANGUAGE.md).

<Steps>

<Step>

### Get the author CLI

The plugins repository contains a command-line tool (CLI) for plugin authors. It runs the same
checks as the app, so you can find mistakes on your computer before anyone installs the plugin.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins
cd pku-harness-plugins
bun install
```

The command has this form: `bun run plugin validate|test|run <plugin-dir> [tool] [json-input]`.

</Step>

<Step>

### Write `PLUGIN.md`

A plugin is one folder, and `PLUGIN.md` is its main file. The file has two parts.

The YAML frontmatter at the top, between the `---` lines, is the _manifest_. It names the plugin,
lists its tools and declares which websites it may reach. The Markdown body below it is written for
the AI assistant. It tells the assistant when and how to use your tools.

```md title="my-classrooms/PLUGIN.md"
---
spec: 1
id: my-classrooms
name: 教室概况
description: 各教学楼现在有多少空闲教室。
version: 0.1.0
author: your-github-name
network: [portal.pku.edu.cn]
tools:
  overview: tools/overview.yaml
i18n:
  en:
    name: Classroom overview
    description: How many classrooms are free in each teaching building right now.
    tools: { overview: { title: Free rooms by building, summary: Free classrooms in each building } }
---

my-classrooms__overview：各楼现在空闲教室数量。用户想找自习的地方时先用它挑楼。
```

`network` lists every public host the plugin may call. A request to any other host fails, so this
list is also what students see before they install. `i18n.en` holds the English text that
English-speaking users see instead of the Chinese.

The app loads only the files the frontmatter names, such as `tools/overview.yaml` here. It never
lists the folder's contents, so you can host the plugin on any static file server.

</Step>

<Step>

### Write the tool

A tool file describes one operation. It has fields for people, a field for the model, a declared
effect, and a list of steps that run in order.

```yaml title="my-classrooms/tools/overview.yaml"
title: 各楼空闲教室数
summary: 各教学楼现在的空闲教室数量
description: 'How many classrooms are free right now in each teaching building: building, free, total.'
effect: read
steps:
  - let: r
    request:
      url: https://portal.pku.edu.cn/publicQuery/classroomQuery/retrClassRoomInfos.do
      headers: { referer: 'https://portal.pku.edu.cn/publicQuery/', accept: 'application/json' }
    as: json
  - check: "r.success && isList(r.rows)"
    error: 教室概况查询未成功
return: |
  {
    buildings: r.rows.map(b => ({ building: b.buildingName, free: b.classroomFree, total: b.classroomSum })),
  }
```

The fields work as follows:

- `title` is the tool's name in the app. Write it in Chinese; the English version goes in
  `i18n.en.tools.overview.title`.
- `summary` is optional. It is one line of at most 80 characters that tells people what the tool
  does, and the app shows it under the title on the install review sheet. Its English version goes
  in `i18n.en.tools.overview.summary`. If you leave that out, the app shows
  English users no summary line.
- `description` is for the model only and is never shown to users. Say what the tool returns and
  when to use it.
- `effect` is `read`, `write`, `money` or `public`. Users decide for each effect whether the
  assistant may run a tool without asking, so the effect must be honest.
- The first step sends the request and binds the parsed JSON to the name `r`. The `check` step
  stops with an error message if the response is not what you expect. `return` builds the result.

Return data, never instructions. The model reads the result as data.

<Callout type="warn" title="Quoting expressions in YAML">
  Put quotes around any expression or `${…}` template that contains `: ` or starts with `{` or `[`.
  Without quotes, YAML reads it as a map or a list instead of a string. `validate` prints a hint
  when this happens.
</Callout>

</Step>

<Step>

### Record a test

A test replays a recorded response instead of calling the real website. It therefore runs offline
and gives the same result every time, even after the campus page changes. Paste a real response,
trimmed to the parts you need, as the `body`. For a long response, save it as a file next to the
test and refer to it with `file:`.

```yaml title="my-classrooms/tests/overview.yaml"
tool: overview
responses:
  - match: retrClassRoomInfos.do
    headers: { content-type: application/json }
    body: '{"success":true,"rows":[{"buildingName":"一教","classroomFree":16,"classroomSum":32}]}'
expect: { buildings: [{ building: 一教, free: 16, total: 32 }] }
```

A test names the `tool` to run. It may also give an `input` and a fixed time, `now`. Under
`responses`, each entry is served to any request whose URL contains the `match` text, and its
content comes from `body` or `file`. For a campus request, also add `campus` with the service name.

Finish the test with one of two fields. `expect` is compared **exactly** with the tool's result.
`expectError` is a pattern that the error message must match.

</Step>

<Step>

### Validate, test and run [#validate-test-run]

```bash
bun run plugin validate path/to/my-classrooms
bun run plugin test path/to/my-classrooms
bun run plugin run path/to/my-classrooms overview '{}'
```

`validate` checks the manifest, the tool schemas, every expression and every file path. These are
the same checks the app and the marketplace run. `test` replays the files in `tests/`. `run`
calls the tool for real, but only for public hosts. Campus requests need the app, because only the
app holds the user's sign-in, so cover them with recorded tests.

</Step>

<Step>

### Share it

Push the folder to a public GitHub repository. The folder's URL is the install link:

```
https://github.com/<you>/<repo>/tree/main/my-classrooms
```

Other students can paste the link in the app, scan its QR code, or open
`pkuharness://plugin?src=<url-encoded link>`. Before anything is installed, the app shows a review
sheet. It says whether the plugin is community or official, lists the websites it can reach (here
`portal.pku.edu.cn`), and shows each tool with its summary and effect.

After that, every `git push` becomes an update. To list the plugin in the marketplace,
[submit the repository](/en/marketplace/submit). One repository can hold any number of plugins. See
[Publishing](/en/docs/marketplace/publishing).

</Step>

</Steps>
